title: Legacy code & replaceable agents
intro: SDD beyond the happy path: brownfield projects, and why your agent is the interchangeable part.

steps.title: Brownfield: reverse-engineer the constitution
steps.body:
On an existing codebase, the constitution isn't written from scratch — the agent **explores the code** (expect a lot of tool calls) plus README, TODO.md, issue trackers, and drafts `mission / tech-stack / roadmap` from what it finds.

The good versions are **honest about gaps** — 'no linter, no CI' goes straight into tech-stack.md — and the roadmap grows out of the existing TODO list. After the commit, the feature loop is **exactly the same** as greenfield.

steps.title: Then replan generously
steps.body:
A freshly SDD-ified legacy project has the most to tune: the first **replanning** pass deserves extra time — testing preferences, roadmap re-cuts, the first skills.

> [!key] The quiz's phrasing: SDD applies to **both** greenfield and brownfield — on legacy code the agent reverse-engineers the constitution and you continue with the normal workflow.

steps.title: The agent is the replaceable part
steps.body: Because the workflow rests on open standards, no single agent owns your project:

points.label: MCP
points.note: Agent ↔ external systems. Any agent reaches the same tools — though for many cases Skills + a CLI are lighter (less setup, lower context cost).

points.label: Skills
points.note: Portable capability folders — the feature-spec skill authored in Claude Code was picked up unchanged by Codex.

points.label: AGENTS.md
points.note: A README for agents (60k+ projects use one) — build/test/convention context any agent can find.

points.label: ACP
points.note: Editor ↔ agent protocol, like LSP: any ACP agent runs in any ACP editor.

steps.title: Choose agents like you choose libraries
steps.body:
The course's demo drove the **same project** — constitution, specs, and the hand-rolled skill — with Claude Code, then Codex, then OpenCode. The agent swapped; nothing else moved.

So pick by evidence (agent scoreboards, code-arena leaderboards) and re-pick freely when something better ships. **Your specs are the durable asset.**

recap:
**Specs outlive both messy codebases and agent market cycles.**

- Brownfield: agent explores code → drafts an honest constitution → normal loop.
- Open standards (MCP, Skills, AGENTS.md, ACP) make agents interchangeable.
- Same project, three agents, zero rework — that's agent-agnostic in practice.
- Choose the best agent per task; keep intent in artifacts you own.
